todos.title: Testing stops after returning from sub-container
todos.description: When using STCheck::debug('test') with nested containers (e.g., bill -> Order), testing completes the sub-container but stops instead of continuing with remaining tables in the parent container

analysis.expectedBehavior: After testing all tables in Order container, should return to bill container and test remaining tables (Article, addressee container)
analysis.actualBehavior: Test stops after completing Order container tables (order, article)
analysis.rootCause: When returning from sub-container, step was set to 10 (delete done), but the condition at line 1138 only checks for step 0 or 11 to trigger makeNextTableContainer_Test(). Step 10 fell through to makeTableListing_Test() which cannot handle it properly.
analysis.fix: Changed step from 10 to 11 when returning from sub-container. Step 11 means 'go to table listing for next table' which correctly triggers makeNextTableContainer_Test() to find the next untested table.

stepsToReproduce: 1. Set STCheck::debug('test') in 04_basic_main.php
2. Run the test - bill container has namedLink to Order container
3. Test completes bill table, jumps into Order container
4. Tests order and article tables in Order container
5. Should return to bill and test Article + addressee, but stops
todos.resolution: Fixed by changing testdebug['step']= 10 to testdebug['step']= 11 at lines 1194, 1201, 1524, 1532

todos.title: Test report shows tables only with test.see debug mode
todos.description: With debug('test') alone, successful table tests are not written to selftable_test_report.txt

analysis.codeSnippet: if(!STCheck::isDebug('test.see')) return ''; // should not write anything into report
analysis.explanation: This is intentional - only errors are logged by default. Use debug('test.see') to see all pages

todos.resolution: This is working as designed. Documentation should clarify the difference between 'test' and 'test.see' modes

todos.title: Add summary statistics to test report
todos.description: The test report should include a summary at the end showing total tables tested, errors found, time per table, etc.

todos.title: Testing does not navigate to needContainer sub-containers when no Article table in main container
todos.description: When the main bill ObjectContainer does not have an Article table defined directly (line 34 commented out in 04_basic_main.php), after returning from the Order sub-container the test declares 'finished' instead of advancing to the addressee container. The bill container has only 1 table so no STChoose-menue-button is rendered, causing makeNextTableContainer_Test() to fall into the else branch which lacked container navigation checks. Additionally, the 'new next table' block in testing() needs safety resets when it finds remaining containers after makeNextTableContainer_Test already declared finished.

analysis.expectedBehavior: After finishing article table in Order container, testing should return to bill container and continue to addressee container, then test Person table
analysis.actualBehavior: After returning from Order to bill, the bill container page has only 1 table (bill) so table['STChoose-menue-button'] is not set. makeNextTableContainer_Test() falls to the else branch which only checked for action['link'] before declaring finished. The container['###link'][0] pointing to addressee existed but was never checked in this code path. The 'new next table' block in testing() also fired but could not override $bFinished=true.
analysis.rootCause: Three issues: (1) The else branch in makeNextTableContainer_Test() (when no table button class exists) only checked for action link then declared finished, without checking for back_tables, older state, or container links. (2) The 'new next table' block's 'more containers' branch did not reset $bFinished and testdebug['status'] when it found a valid container link, so $bFinished=true from makeNextTableContainer_Test persisted. (3) Step was set to 0 instead of -1 in the 'more containers' branch.
analysis.fix: Fix 1: Added guard '&& testdebug[link-type] != container_link' to 'new next table' block at line 1174. Fix 2: Added container navigation branch in makeNextTableContainer_Test() 'noTable' path (line 1570). Fix 3: Added full navigation chain (back_tables, older, container links) to the else branch of makeNextTableContainer_Test() (line 1612-1653) so that when no table buttons exist, the code still checks for parent container back-navigation and needContainer sub-containers before declaring finished. Fix 4: In 'more containers' branch of 'new next table' block (line 1198), added $bFinished=false and status='running' reset, and changed step from 0 to -1.

stepsToReproduce: 1. In 04_basic_main.php, comment out line 34: $main->needTable('Article')
2. Set STCheck::debug('test.see.develop')
3. Run the test - bill container still has namedLink to Order container and needContainer($addressee)
4. Test completes bill table, jumps into Order container via namedLink
5. Tests order and article tables in Order container
6. Returns to bill but restarts bill table test instead of navigating to addressee
todos.resolution: Four changes in STSiteCreator.php: (1) Guard 'new next table' at line 1174 with link-type != container_link. (2) In 'more containers' branch at line 1198, reset $bFinished=false and status='running' when container link found, change step from 0 to -1. (3) Added container['###link'] check in makeNextTableContainer_Test() 'noTable' path at line 1570. (4) Added full navigation chain (back_tables, older, containers) to the else branch at line 1612, so when no table buttons exist (single-table container), the code navigates to sub-containers instead of declaring finished.

todos.title: Test loops infinitely between bill and addressee containers
todos.description: After ISSUE-004 fix, when all containers in bill (Order + addressee) have been tested, the test returns to bill but re-enters addressee endlessly. The container['###link'] checks added in ISSUE-004 did not verify whether cont_count >= containers before navigating to a sub-container. Since the addressee needContainer link is always present in the bill page HTML, the code re-enters it on every cycle with cont_count incrementing (2,3,4,...) past containers=2.

analysis.expectedBehavior: After addressee container finishes (5 tables: person, country, state, county, address), test returns to bill with cont_count=2, containers=2 and declares finished
analysis.actualBehavior: After addressee returns to bill (cont_count=2, containers=2), the container['###link'] check finds the addressee link still present in HTML, navigates to it again, increments cont_count to 3, and loops indefinitely
analysis.rootCause: The container['###link'] elseif conditions in both the 'noTable' path and the 'else' branch of makeNextTableContainer_Test() only checked whether any container links existed in the page HTML, without checking whether all containers had already been tested (cont_count >= containers). The link is always present because it's a needContainer button rendered by the framework.
analysis.fix: Added guards 'isset($testdebug[containers]) && $testdebug[containers] > 0 && $testdebug[cont_count] < $testdebug[containers]' to both container['###link'] elseif conditions. When cont_count >= containers (e.g. 2 >= 2), the condition is false and execution falls through to the 'finished' branch.

stepsToReproduce: 1. In 04_basic_main.php, comment out line 34: $main->needTable('Article')
2. Set STCheck::debug('test.see.develop')
3. Run the test - bill tests Order then addressee
4. After addressee finishes all 5 tables, test returns to bill
5. Bill re-enters addressee instead of declaring finished
6. Loop repeats indefinitely (test report grows to 13000+ lines)
todos.resolution: Added cont_count < containers guard to two container['###link'] elseif conditions in makeNextTableContainer_Test(): (1) 'noTable' path at line ~1575, (2) 'else' branch at line ~1641. Both now require isset(containers) && containers > 0 && cont_count < containers before navigating to sub-containers.

todos.title: Test report end summary missing for sub-containers (Order, addressee)
todos.description: When testing nested containers (bill -> Order, bill -> addressee), the test report step entries show all containers being tested correctly, but the final summary only shows the top-level container (bill). The summaries for sub-containers Order and addressee are missing from the report.

analysis.expectedBehavior: Each sub-container (Order, addressee) should have its own summary in the test report showing how many tables were tested and their status, similar to the final summary for the top-level container.
analysis.actualBehavior: Only the top-level container (bill) gets a summary via writeEndTimeReport() when $bFinished=true. Sub-containers finish by calling restoreDebugOlder() which replaces their testdebug state with the parent's, losing the sub-container's progress data without ever writing a summary.
analysis.rootCause: restoreDebugOlder() replaces the sub-container's testdebug (including container name, tested tables, and progress) with the parent's saved state. No summary data is saved before this restoration. writeEndTimeReport() is only called when $bFinished=true at the end of the entire test. Additionally, each test step is a separate PHP page request, so instance properties are lost between requests - only testdebug data (passed via URL parameters) persists.
analysis.fix: Two changes: (1) Modified restoreDebugOlder() to save sub-container summary data (container name, tables count, testedTables, tablesWithFaults, faults flag) as an array entry in testdebug['subContainerReports'] before restoring the parent state. Since this key is not in aDebugShiftVars, it persists across push/restore cycles and across page requests. (2) Modified writeEndTimeReport() to iterate over testdebug['subContainerReports'] and render each sub-container's summary inside the 'Test finished' end block, before the main container summary.

stepsToReproduce: 1. Set STCheck::debug('test.see') in 04_basic_main.php
2. Run the test - bill container has namedLink to Order and needContainer($addressee)
3. Test runs through all containers: bill, Order(order,article), bill(article), addressee(person,country,state,county,address)
4. Check selftable_test_report.txt - only bill container has end summary
5. Order and addressee summaries are missing
todos.resolution: Sub-container summary data is now stored in testdebug['subContainerReports'] array (survives page requests via URL parameters). restoreDebugOlder() saves summary data before restoring parent state. writeEndTimeReport() renders all sub-container summaries inside the 'Test finished' end block.

todos.title: Refactor STSiteCreator::testing() into focused helper methods
todos.description: The testing() method was a monolithic ~420-line method mixing initialization, dispatch, navigation, reporting, debug output, error handling, and file writing. Refactored into 15 focused private methods while preserving all existing behavior.

problemsBefore: Deep nesting (5+ levels of if/else blocks)

extractedMethods.canContinueTesting(): Checks if test can proceed based on SiteCreator result and status
extractedMethods.isSuccessfulResult(): Checks if result is NOERROR or BOXDISPLAY
extractedMethods.sortTestLinks(): Sorts global test links by aTestTypes order
extractedMethods.initializeOrContinueTest(): Starts new test or continues from existing state
extractedMethods.adjustStepForPendingAction(): Handles pending JS action steps (4/7) and step 0->1
extractedMethods.dispatchTestStep(): Routes to makeNextTableContainer_Test, makeTableListing_Test, or makeTableAction_Test
extractedMethods.finalizeDoubleUpdate(): Resets DoubleUpdate flags when both runs complete
extractedMethods.handleTableTransition(): Manages transitions between tables and containers
extractedMethods.collectTestStepReport(): Gathers output buffer and writes step report
extractedMethods.advanceStep(): Increments step counter with DoubleUpdate rollback support
extractedMethods.outputTestDebugInfo(): Shows debug info when extended debug modes are active
extractedMethods.buildTestNavigation(): Creates JavaScript for page navigation (link, edit, action types)
extractedMethods.buildTestExceptionReport(): Builds exception report and shows error on screen

analysis.testingMethodAfter: ~55 lines, clear orchestration flow with descriptive method calls

todos.title: Person update form does not preselect stored self-FK spouse entry
todos.description: In examples/test/03_basic_display.php, opening the Person table in UPDATE mode can show the spouse field with only the default 'entry can be null' option selected although the row contains a non-null spouse foreign key. The same failure makes the update box appear to fall back to the first dropdown entry instead of the stored relation.

analysis.expectedBehavior: When updating a Person row such as Jane Doe, the spouse select field should preselect the stored Person reference. Other FK dropdowns should continue to use the current row value rather than the browser's first fallback entry.
analysis.actualBehavior: The Person update form first failed with 'no where-clausel defined to display' although the update URL contained a valid Person limitation. After that, the spouse dropdown stayed on the default null placeholder and in some cases displayed only the current Person row or visible numeric IDs instead of the configured identification columns.
analysis.rootCause: The problem had three cooperating causes. First, own-table query limitation lookup in STBaseTable::modifyQueryLimitation() used the current table name with case-sensitive matching, while the request on macOS/MariaDB carried lowercase table keys such as 'person'. That prevented the update box from rebuilding its where clause. Second, STItemBox::getJoinArray() tried to preselect FK options by comparing displayed aliases from the join rows with aliases from the update row, which does not work for the self-referential Person spouse field because the dropdown rows use identification aliases while the update row stores the FK value under the selected alias. Third, the self-FK dropdown could be built from a limited helper table object, and when the PK column had to be added for internal matching it was added as a visible identification column instead of hidden metadata.
analysis.implementedFix: STBaseTable::modifyQueryLimitation() now resolves query limitations using the database case-sensitivity rule from hasLowerCaseTableNames() and only falls back to lowercase matching when the database is not case-sensitive. STBaseTable::clearQueryLimitation() was added so derived helper tables can explicitly drop inherited query limitation state. STItemBox::getJoinArray() now detects self-referential FKs by table name, clones the current table configuration for the spouse dropdown, clears inherited query limitation state on that helper table, keeps the PK as hidden identification data with getIdentif(), and determines the selected spouse option from the stored FK value using the selected alias path and HTML field name.
analysis.validationStatus: Editor diagnostics report no errors in STBaseTable.php, STItemBox.php, and STQueryString.php. Manual browser validation on examples/test/03_basic_display.php confirmed that the update form now opens correctly, the spouse dropdown lists Person entries by the configured identification columns, and the stored spouse entry is preselected. PHP CLI validation could not be executed in this environment because the 'php' command is unavailable.

stepsToReproduce: 1. Open examples/test/03_basic_display.php with the sample database from examples/00__mariaDB_tables.sql
2. Navigate to the Person table and open Jane Doe in UPDATE mode
3. Observe that Address can still resolve correctly but the spouse dropdown stays on the null placeholder instead of the stored spouse entry
4. Observe that the update box appears to use the first available dropdown entry when no option is marked selected
todos.resolution: Resolved by combining a database-aware query-limitation lookup in STBaseTable::modifyQueryLimitation() with a self-FK-specific dropdown fix in STItemBox::getJoinArray(). The update form now rebuilds its Person where clause correctly on macOS/MariaDB, the spouse dropdown shows all Person entries by identification columns, and the stored spouse value is preselected.
